model_metadata:
### Model stg_customers
File: models/staging/stg_customers.sql · materialized as view
Description: Cleaned customers, one row per customer. Email lower-cased, country code upper-cased.
Columns (name · type in warehouse · description · tests):
- customer_id · INTEGER · Primary key of the customer. · tests: unique, not_null
- first_name · VARCHAR · Customer first name.
- last_name · VARCHAR · Customer last name.
- email · VARCHAR · Lower-cased email address. A small share of missing emails is tolerated (max 5%). · tests: null_rate_below(max_rate=0.05)
- country_code · VARCHAR · Upper-cased ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (from raw_customers.country). · tests: not_null
- created_at · TIMESTAMP · UTC timestamp when the account was created.
- loaded_at · TIMESTAMP · UTC timestamp when the row was loaded into the warehouse.
SQL (models/staging/stg_customers.sql):
```sql
with source as (

    select * from {{ source('raw', 'raw_customers') }}

),

renamed as (

    select
        customer_id,
        first_name,
        last_name,
        lower(email) as email,
        upper(country) as country_code,
        cast(created_at as timestamp) as created_at,
        loaded_at
    from source

)

select * from renamed
```

Downstream nodes (affected if the failing node is wrong or skipped):
- model dim_customers (table): One row per customer with order history and lifetime value. Used by marketing and finance dashboards.
- exposure finance_revenue_dashboard (dashboard, owner: Finance analytics): Daily revenue by payment method and order status. Refreshed at 07:00 UTC and used in the daily finance stand-up.
- exposure marketing_customer_dashboard (dashboard, owner: Marketing analytics): Customer counts, lifetime value and repeat-purchase rate by country.
Column-level lineage (as designed):
- stg_customers.customer_id ← raw_customers.customer_id

- stg_customers.email ← raw_customers.email (lower-cased)
- stg_customers.country_code ← raw_customers.country (upper-cased)
- dim_customers.{customer_id, first_name, last_name, email, country_code, created_at} ← stg_customers (same names)
- dim_customers.{first_order_date, most_recent_order_date, number_of_orders} ← stg_orders.order_date / order_id, per customer_id

gold_standard_remediation.root_cause: raw.raw_customers has 3 customer_ids that appear twice (17, 58, 121): the original row and a second row with a different email, loaded at 2026-10-25 14:50 UTC. The CRM account-merge job enabled yesterday writes the merged account as a new row with the same customer_id instead of updating the existing one. stg_customers passes both rows through, so unique fails on stg_customers.customer_id and dim_customers and its tests are skipped.
gold_standard_remediation.fix: Ask the CRM team to make the merge job update the existing account (upsert on customer_id) and remove the extra rows. Until then, keep one row per customer in models/staging/stg_customers.sql: add `qualify row_number() over (partition by customer_id order by loaded_at desc) = 1`, so the most recently loaded (merged) version wins.
gold_standard_remediation.verification: `select customer_id, count(*) from stg_customers group by 1 having count(*) > 1` returns no rows, and `dbt build --select stg_customers+` passes with dim_customers back to 200 rows.
gold_standard_remediation.text:
Root cause: raw.raw_customers has 3 customer_ids that appear twice (17, 58, 121): the original row and a second row with a different email, loaded at 2026-10-25 14:50 UTC. The CRM account-merge job enabled yesterday writes the merged account as a new row with the same customer_id instead of updating the existing one. stg_customers passes both rows through, so unique fails on stg_customers.customer_id and dim_customers and its tests are skipped.

Fix: Ask the CRM team to make the merge job update the existing account (upsert on customer_id) and remove the extra rows. Until then, keep one row per customer in models/staging/stg_customers.sql: add `qualify row_number() over (partition by customer_id order by loaded_at desc) = 1`, so the most recently loaded (merged) version wins.

Verification: `select customer_id, count(*) from stg_customers group by 1 having count(*) > 1` returns no rows, and `dbt build --select stg_customers+` passes with dim_customers back to 200 rows.
